reason: E3 supports the substrate sensitivity and the advantage of low-heat-input laser repair for Cr-Ni-Mo steels. E1 directly supports the improved hardness, wear, and corrosion resistance of a similar HEA+WC+CeO2 coating. E2 only provides general background on laser cladding benefits for H13 steel, not the specific HEA composite or hot cracking reduction. The key premise of reduced hot cracking is not directly supported by any cited evidence.
premises: Laser cladding provides rapid solidification and low heat input, yielding a refined microstructure and narrow HAZ
High-entropy alloy composite with WC and CeO2 additives refines grains and strengthens grain boundaries
The refined microstructure and hard phases enhance surface hardness, wear resistance, and corrosion resistance
The approach reduces hot cracking susceptibility compared to traditional fusion welding
The substrate material (quenched and tempered Cr-Ni-Mo steel) is sensitive to high-temperature cracking and benefits from low-heat-input repair
